definitions.gloss: analogy; inference by analogy; analogical reasoning
definitions.explanation: The process of reasoning from known similarities to infer additional similarities. Drawing conclusions about something based on its resemblance to something else.

examples.japanese: {類推|るいすい}から{判断|はんだん}する。
{過去|かこ}の{事例|じれい}から{類推|るいすい}すると、{同|おな}じ{結果|けっか}になるだろう。
examples.english: Reasoning by analogy from past cases, the result will likely be the same.

examples.japanese: {他|ほか}の{言語|げんご}の{知識|ちしき}から{類推|るいすい}して、{新|あたら}しい{言語|げんご}の{文法|ぶんぽう}を{理解|りかい}しようとした。
examples.english: I tried to understand the grammar of the new language by drawing analogies from my knowledge of other languages.

notes:
USAGE:
Used as a suru verb ({類推|るいすい}する). Common in academic, logical, and linguistic contexts. In linguistics, {類推|るいすい} refers to the process by which irregular forms are regularized based on patterns from similar words.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {類推|るいすい}する (to reason by analogy)
- {類推|るいすい}から (from analogy)
- {類推|るいすい}{解釈|かいしゃく} (analogical interpretation)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {推測|すいそく}: conjecture, guess — broader meaning, not necessarily based on analogy
- {推論|すいろん}: inference, deduction — more general logical reasoning
